_comment: Player-facing update notes, newest first. The homepage Updates tab and the in-game "what's new" popup both render from this file. Add an entry with anything players will notice. size: "major" shows highlights in the popup even when it isn't the newest missed; "minor" shows one line.

updates.title: A Map in the Wiki, and Paladins and Rangers by the Book
updates.summary: The wiki has a world map and how-the-game-works guides, and paladins and rangers cast as they do in 5e.
highlights: The wiki has a painted world map with every town and road pinned on it, and new guides to combat, survival, day and night, learning spells, scribing and Homeward Stones
Every scroll has a wiki page, and spell pages say who learns them, where to scribe them and what drops them
Paladins and rangers follow 5e: their spells begin at level 2. Paladins know the whole paladin list from then on; rangers learn 2 spells at level 2 and more as they level
Hunger reads the same everywhere: Starving, Hungry, Well Fed, Stuffed

updates.title: Armor You Can Wear, and Gear You Can Buy
updates.summary: Armor shops sell the pieces you actually wear, and acid, caltrops, ball bearings and whetstones are on the shelves.
highlights: Armor shops sold whole sets that couldn't be worn. They now sell each piece (a hauberk and chausses, a cuirass and greaves) to wear together
Caltrops and ball bearings at the general stores, acid in the Kingdom and at Verdant's Green Mortar, whetstones at the forges and Ironpeak's mining supplier
Goldenhaven's town music now unlocks when you arrive, and Dusthaven, Frosthold and Saltwind have music of their own
Windows like Allocate Points, the level guide and the shop have a solid background again and fit on screen, scrolling when they're long
The Stats tab lists the feats you've taken

updates.title: Homeward Stones and the Waystones
updates.summary: Teleport home with a Homeward Stone, wake the ancient waystones to travel between cities, and take the ferry on the water roads.
highlights: Every character has a Homeward Stone for their home city: use it from your inventory to return to the waystone in its town square, once a week, with no time passing. Started before today? Ask your home city's vault keeper about Homeward Stones to claim yours
Lost your stone? Your home keeper sells another. Earn a keeper's trust in their own quest and they'll sell you their city's stone too

The six starting cities each have a waystone in the town square. Magister Corvin Ashgrove at the Kingdom's Mage Tower knows how to wake them: a quest chain from level 5 to 15. Woken waystones carry you between each other once a week
Six new stone quests, one for each starting city (except your own), from level 3
A ferryman on the Shadowmere Wetlands and Suncrest Coastlands roads will carry you a good way along, for a fee
Combat dice: a crit or a 2d6 shows every die, and advantage or disadvantage shows both d20s, the dropped one faded
The healer's kit (and anything else you can use up) now has a Use option. Acid, nets and caltrops wait for a fight instead of being wasted
Reloading your last save from Settings now rolls the clock back too

updates.title: Scrolls in the Wild, and Wizards Who Remember
updates.summary: Scrolls drop from spellcasting foes and old treasure, two shops sell the basics, and wizards can commit a scroll to memory.
highlights: Scrolls turn up as loot from spellcasting foes and in old treasure: everyday spells often, stronger ones rarely
The court arcanist at the Mage Tower and the almoner at the Dawnflame temple sell a few basic scrolls
Wizards: keep a scroll in your spellbook and choose Commit to memory to learn its spell for good (gold and time per spell level; the scroll is used up)

updates.title: Scribe Your Own Scrolls
updates.summary: Casters can scribe scrolls of any spell they know, at a temple, a shrine, the Green Mortar or the Mage Tower.
highlights: Clerics and paladins scribe at the Temple of the Dawnflame and the shrines in Dusthaven and Saltwind; druids and rangers at the Green Mortar in Verdant; wizards, sorcerers, warlocks and bards at the Kingdom's Mage Tower
A scroll takes parchment, the spell's own component, gold and a few hours, and you need ink and a pen on you
Your casting ability sets the chance. A failed attempt still spends the materials
Any caster can read any scroll: it casts the spell for its mana and is used up

updates.title: Casters Learn as They Level
updates.summary: Casters gain spells as they level (druids and clerics learn their whole list, the rest pick), and every caster gets the spell slots their level grants.
highlights: Druids and clerics know every class spell of each spell level they reach: a level-3 druid gets barkskin, moonbeam, hold person, lesser restoration and pass without trace
Bards, sorcerers, warlocks, paladins, rangers and wizards learn new spells as they level: pick them in the Learn spells list when you allocate points
Spell slots grow with your level (they were stuck at level-1 counts). Existing characters catch up the next time they load in

updates.title: New to Nostr? Your Saves Have a Home
updates.summary: Players without a relay list of their own now save to four default public relays (offchain.pub, relay.ditto.pub, relay.nostr.net, nos.lol). Settings can make them your list in one click.
highlights: Saves from a brand-new key go to the game's default relays instead of being refused
Settings → Your Relays shows the defaults and can make them your published list

updates.title: Gear That Does Something
updates.summary: Throw acid and nets, scatter caltrops, poison your blade, and a dozen idle items find a use.
highlights: Throw acid (2d6), alchemist's fire (it keeps burning) or a net (it pins a foe in place) at your target
Scatter caltrops or ball bearings between you and a foe: whatever steps on them is stopped, hurt or knocked down. Mind your own feet
Coat your blade with basic poison (+1d4 for 3 hits), or hone it with a whetstone before a fight (+1 damage, and the stone isn't used up)
Thrown and ranged weapons no longer roll at disadvantage at every range, and reach weapons strike two squares away
A candle lights your off hand, the climber's kit adds +2 Athletics, and Bob at the Salty Anchor pays for the Rat King's tails
Gone from the shops: the 10-foot pole, the chain and the hourglass

updates.title: Fixes: HP Bars, Quest Turn-ins & Road Fights
updates.summary: HP bars move on every hit, finished quests say so, and road quest fights wait until you're travelling.
highlights: HP bars update the moment a hit lands, spells included
Finishing a quest shows "Quest complete" and the journal updates at once
Quest fights waiting on a road find you while you travel, not the instant you load in

updates.title: Nine New Quests
updates.summary: Nine quests are playable, with seven new monsters, new rewards that are worth wearing, and dice that tell you what they are.
highlights: The Missing Mule: Thistle's mule bolted up the Cragspire pass. Find her at the new Mountain Pass Overlook, past a wolf pack and its dire-wolf leader
The Missing Heirloom: bandits hold the old watchtower, and the Mayor's signet is hidden upstairs. Reward: a Ring of Protection
The Black Flame continues the main story: a hidden cellar, cultists, and the Shadow Stalker. Reward: the Amulet of Light, a light you wear
The Shadow's Source: the Sunken Temple's drowned sanctum, and the Eye of the Abyss cleansed at the Raven Shrine
Class and race quests: The Paladin's Vow, The Rogue's Shadow Trial, The Axe of the Ancestors for dwarves, and Elven Heritage for elves
Daily bounties from any vault keeper: Highway Rats and the Cragspire Survey
New monsters: dire wolf, restless spirit, shadow stalker, kobold warrior and shaman, shadow tentacle, corrupted dryad
Combat dice show their shape and type (d4 to d100) and who is rolling, and damage lines name their dice
Rings can be worn, and NPCs can answer to your race, class, stats and skills

updates.title: Day, Night & Every Spell
updates.summary: Time flows on its own, night is dangerous, and every spell does something.
highlights: The clock runs by default and stops itself when something needs you: a fight, a discovery, hunger or tiredness setting in
Time runs at half speed in town, so there's room to shop and talk
Night falls: undead and shapeshifters roam, road fights come more often, and without darkvision or a torch in hand you fight at disadvantage. Fights pay 25% more XP until dawn
Torches, lamps and lanterns can be held in your off hand
Every spell has an effect in play, 23 new spells arrive, area spells hit everything in the area, and spells respect their range
A loading screen with sayings while the world wakes, and a saves screen that lists your saves at once
The vault works like a bank, and the clock holds while you're at the vault, in a shop or in conversation
Right-click anything for its wiki page
You're warned to save before the server restarts for an update

updates.title: Monsters, Loot & a Town Full of Shops
updates.summary: 36 new monsters, rebuilt loot, and eleven new shopkeepers.
highlights: 36 new monsters for levels 1–5: every road now has something new to meet, from hyenas and giant crabs to kuo-toa, worgs, specters and hippogriffs
Enemy spellcasters — cultists, acolytes, apprentice wizards, cult fanatics and druids — and the wands, orbs and spellbooks they carry
Every monster has a sprite, and every item has art
Loot rebuilt: purses follow the 5e treasure tables, creatures drop their parts (spider silk, bone dust, spirit dust), and the best gear — plate, greatswords, rare foci — is found, never bought

11 new shopkeepers: the Grand Forge, the Mage Tower, a dwarven crossbow forge, an elven bowyer, an herbalist, the Dawnflame almonry, the Golden Bazaar, an orc war-gear trader, and the first shops in Dusthaven, Frosthold and Saltwind
General stores carry one dependable list of travel basics, and potions come back slowly instead of all at once
Survival matters on the road: it sets how fast you travel and gives you a roll to spot an ambush before it springs. A navigator's kit or a spyglass helps
Useful odds and ends: healer's kits bind wounds, perfume sweetens prices, a tackle box keeps the fish smell contained
A community wiki at /wiki, built straight from the game's data

updates.title: Locks, Secrets & Smarter Fights
updates.summary: Keys and lockpicking, the first main quest, and combat terrain.
highlights: Keys and locks: locked rooms and chests, a keyring for your keys, lockpicks that break, and Tumblers — a lockpicking minigame
The Rising Shadow is playable: meet the Oracle in the new Temple of the Dawnflame and follow the main quest's first chapter
The Rats of Goldenhaven: down into the sewers to face the Rat King
Hidden places in every city, found by spending time in a district
Combat terrain: rough ground, water, cover and high ground, with line of sight and monsters that use it
Stealth openings: catch monsters unaware and sneak past, strike first, or walk up — or get ambushed yourself
Fight several enemies at once, in true initiative order
Fairer fights at low levels, gentler downing, and death saves you can watch
Use what's at hand: only items in your quick slots are free in combat — digging in your pack costs a bonus action
Lose a fight and you can reload your last save instead of taking the loss

updates.title: Friends, Parties & Saves on Nostr
updates.summary: Other players, chat and whispers, parties, and saves on your relays.
highlights: See who else is playing: players at your spot, travellers on your road, and a Friends panel built from your Nostr follows
Chat — say, area and party — and private whispers sent as encrypted Nostr DMs, sealed in your browser
Parties of up to five: travel together, sleep together, and fight together in shared turn-based battles with flanking, healing and help actions
Your saves can live on Nostr relays: signed by you, loadable anywhere, checked by the official server
Character portraits — describe one, link one, or upload one — and a unique crest for every npub
Proof-of-key login: you prove you hold your key, and all signing stays in your browser
Your Nostr profile and relays, viewable and editable in game
Quest journal reworked: sortable, filterable, with a badges tab

updates.title: Feats, Scrolls, Gathering & a Web App
updates.summary: Feats at level-up, spell scrolls, gathering, a new sign-in, and an installable app.
highlights: Feats — take a feat instead of ability points at level-up (Tough, War Caster, Elemental Adept, and the stat feats)
Spell scrolls — read a scroll to cast its spell in or out of combat (still costs mana, no preparation needed)
Gathering & lockpicking — mining and fishing nodes and locked chests, worked with the right tool and a skill check, with tiered loot
New MILL sign-in — one modal for every Nostr login (extension, Amber, remote bunker, private key, or a brand-new identity); all signing stays in your browser
Installable as an app — add Pubkey Quest to your home screen, and links now unfurl with a preview card
Mobile polish and bug fixes ahead of open testing

updates.title: The Adventure Comes Alive
updates.summary: Quests, dungeons, encounters, real spellcasting and levelling up.
highlights: Quests, dungeons & encounters are playable — pick up quests from NPCs and boards, explore points of interest as branching node-walks, and hit random and hand-authored encounters while travelling
Rotating daily quests handed out by innkeepers
Spellcasting is real — cast spells in and out of combat with mana and material components, and drink potions or throw items mid-fight
Combat depth — class abilities (Rage, Second Wind, Ki…), conditions (poisoned, prone, frightened…), and saving throws
Character progression — level up from XP, spend ability points, and grow your HP and mana
Building interiors — enter inns and taverns, rent a room, and sleep the night

updates.title: Project Rebrand & Effects Polish
updates.summary: Nostr Hero becomes Pubkey Quest, and worn items and consumables apply their effects.
highlights: Complete rebrand from Nostr Hero to Pubkey Quest
Worn item effects system (armor/weapons apply stat bonuses)
Consumable items fixed (food, potions apply effects correctly)
Effects system now fully data-driven via CODEX
Weight system cleanup and optimization
Inventory delta system fix (no more full re-renders)

updates.title: CODEX Expansion & Architecture
updates.summary: Content tools, a restructured codebase, and automatic deploys.
highlights: CODEX Starting Gear Editor (edit class equipment visually)
CODEX Systems/Effects Editor (manage all 27+ game effects)
Massive effects system refactor and CODEX integration
Major repository restructure (clean game module organization)
CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions, auto-deploy to test server)
API documentation setup (Swagger)
Item database improvements and validation

updates.title: Shops, NPCs & Game Systems
updates.summary: Merchants, NPC schedules, vaults, resting, music and the day/night clock.
highlights: Full merchant system (buy/sell, charisma scaling, gold tracking, restocks)
NPC schedule system with time-aware dialogue
Vault storage system (per-city secure storage)
Wait/rest system with inn/tavern integration
Music system with location-based tracks
New time system with day/night cycle
Delta architecture (surgical DOM updates, backend-authoritative)
Effects system first implementation (hunger, fatigue, status conditions)
Stats tab, abilities tab, equipment refactors
Massive Go code reorganization (api → game modules)
ES6 module migration with Vite build system
CODEX initial implementation (item editor, migration, validation)
Multiple frontend cleanup passes (dead code removal, JS consolidation)
